help.title: How to use
help.hint: Find your way around and understand terms
help.vst.body: Install a VST3 plugin using the steps from its distributor. Many plugins install into the standard folders. “Add VST” searches those folders and any place you add in “Folders to search”. After installing, press “Find VSTs” when nothing is registered yet, or “Rescan all” when plugins are already listed.
help.home.stage.title: Current status (see whether your voice is coming through)
help.home.stage.musicTitle: Current status (see whether sound is playing)
help.home.stage.1: When Sing or Talk is saved, Current status shows “{mode}” and the name, and when neither is saved the heading is “{currentVoice}”. It also shows whether sound is coming in and “{send}”, and “{notSending}” appears only when the output is muted or the volume is zero.
help.home.stage.2: The heading is “{musicHeading}”, with “{listen}”. The path appears once, at the top of the screen, but on Home at 1400px wide or more it appears once in the “{check}” diagram in the right column instead.
help.home.stage.muteMusic: When the output is muted or the volume is zero, it says “{notPlaying}”. The cause and the way to release it are in “{muteCause}” on Output in the right column.
help.home.stage.muteCause: The cause and the way to release it are in “{muteCause}” on Output in the right column.
help.home.stage.3: The status display, elapsed time, and audio path are at the top of the screen. On Home, when the window is 1400px wide or more, only the audio path is in the “{check}” diagram in the right column instead.
help.home.stage.modes: The “{singing}” and “{talk}” switch is at the top of the screen too.
help.home.stage.4: “{lock}” is on the right side of the screen.
help.home.stage.lockMusic: “{lock}” appears on the right side of the screen only while locked.
help.home.stage.5: Voice flow appears once sound starts coming in after you start audio. When audio is stopped or waiting, Current status shows the state.
help.home.stage.flowMusic: “{flow}” appears after “{startListening}”, once sound starts coming in. When audio is stopped or waiting, Current status shows the state.
help.home.stage.6: When setup is already finished, the order matches Sing / Talk: Current status, “{flow}”, “{musicSound}”, then “{musicPlayback}” only when a setup is saved, then “{check}”.
help.home.stage.7: “{musicPlayback}” only switches saved setups. The connection method and sample rate are in “{history}” under “{check}”.
help.home.meters.title: Microphone and output meters (check the level)
help.home.meters.musicTitle: Playback source and output meters (check the level)
help.home.meters.1: On the right side of the screen, “{input}” is the bar for incoming sound. “{output}” is the number labeled “{peakLabel}”.
help.home.meters.music: On the right side of the screen, “{source}” is the bar for incoming sound. “{output}” is the number labeled “{peakLabel}”.
help.home.meters.2: The level sent onward is the “{send}” bar on Current status. While stopped, waiting, or no longer updating, the in-range tint stays off.
help.home.meters.listen: The level you hear is the “{listen}” bar on Current status. While stopped, waiting, or no longer updating, the in-range tint stays off.
help.home.meters.3: The bar follows the current level, and the output number on the right side of the screen holds a recent peak.
help.home.meters.4: Moving meters do not confirm that someone else can hear you.
help.home.meters.5: Incoming sound is shown on the input bar at the right, at the current level and without delay. Voice flow compares the sound before and after processing.
help.home.meters.incomingMusic: Incoming sound is shown on the input bar at the right, at the current level and without delay. “{flow}” compares the sound before and after processing.
help.home.sound.title: Sound adjustments (shape noise and voice)
help.home.sound.musicTitle: Shape the sound (process with a VST)
help.home.sound.1: “{noise}” targets steady noise such as fans, and does not fully remove speech or music.
help.home.sound.2: Use “{voice}” or VST effects to adjust your voice, then listen with Voice Check.
help.home.sound.4: When you make the window taller, the cards also show “{measure}”, the voice type, and controls that open each VST. On a short window, open the Sound page from “{tierLink}”
help.home.sound.5: When no VST is loaded, open the page with “{add}”. Otherwise use “{openVst}”.
help.home.sound.6: The Sound page is split into “{basic}”, “{modes}”, “{singingSection}”, and “{peak}”.
help.home.sound.7: On and off for “{peak}” is the switch beside the heading. Ceiling and release are in “{peakDetails}”.
help.home.sound.9: The standard folders cannot be removed. Add other places from “Folders to search”.
help.home.check.1: “{check}” leads to connection and destination checks.
help.home.check.2: On a wide window, the connection column opens on the right of Home. On a narrow window, open it from “{details}” below.
help.home.check.3: Hearing your own voice and confirming sound in your streaming or calling app are separate checks.
help.home.check.4: The name of the input or source selected in the receiving app stays off Home, and diagnosis asks for it when the receiving-app checklist appears. You can leave it blank and still continue.
help.home.check.5: “{check}” holds “{diagnose}” at the top, the audio-flow diagram, “{change}” on the destination row, and “{changeDevices}”. The check box and “{setup}” are inside the closed “{history}”.
help.home.check.6: Only when preparation has a problem, “{configure}” or “{refresh}” appears to the right of “{changeDevices}”.
help.home.check.7: “{change}” opens a menu to choose the destination again. The audio route does not change; how you check it and what is shown change, and the saved receiver name is cleared.
help.home.check.8: Until you choose a destination, the four choices stay open instead of the menu.
help.home.check.musicStructure: “{check}” holds “{diagnose}”, the audio-flow diagram, and “{changeDevices}”. The connection method and sample rate are inside the closed “{history}”.
help.home.check.musicListen: “{listenCheck}” is on the top band, not here.
help.home.check.title: Check the connection (see whether it gets through)
help.home.check.musicTitle: Check the connection (see whether it is connected)
help.home.footer.title: Live controls on the right of the screen (stop or compare the sound)
help.home.footer.musicTitle: Controls on the right of the screen (stop or compare the sound)
help.home.footer.1: The right side of the screen runs from “{mute}”, microphone volume, “{gain}”, and “{compare}” to “{lock}”.
help.home.footer.2: “{compare}” bypasses external VST effects; noise reduction and voice shaping continue.
help.home.footer.music: The right side of the screen runs from “{mute}”, “{sourceGain}”, and “{gain}” to “{compare}”. “{lock}” also appears while locked.
help.home.footer.3: While audio is stopped, “{compare}” cannot be pressed. The reason is tied to the switch.
help.home.other: The overview for the other use appears when you switch “{usage}” on “{connect}”.
help.setup.voice.1: In the Setup that opens first, choose Use and your microphone. If you closed it, open it again from “{setup}” in “{history}” under “{check}”.
help.setup.voice.2: If the status on the top band says “{running}”, audio is already on. If it is stopped, press “{startAudio}” on Home.
help.setup.voice.3: In OBS, the audio input capture meter moving with your voice means it arrived. In a calling app, check its input meter. With “{ownVoice}”, check by hearing your voice.
help.setup.voice.trouble: If it does not arrive, see “{receiver}” in “{trouble}”.
help.setup.music.1: In the Setup that opens first, choose “{music}” for Use, then your playback source and listening device. If you closed it, open it again from “{setup}” in “{history}” under “{check}”.
help.setup.music.2: If the status on the top band says “{running}”, audio is already on. If it is stopped, press “{startListening}” on Home.
help.setup.music.3: Play a song in your music app. If you hear it on your own headphones or speakers and the “{source}” bar on the right of the screen moves, sound is coming in. When you have added a VST, press “{compare}” to compare; if the sound changes, the VST is applied.
help.setup.music.trouble: If there is no sound, see “{silent}” in “{trouble}”.
help.setup.body: The setup steps run “{wizardUsage}” → “{wizardInput}” → “{wizardOutput}” → “{wizardCheck}” and decide how to use Auralyn and route sound. For music, the second step is “{wizardSource}”. Choosing “{music}” on the first screen sets up listening to PC audio with a VST. “{ownVoice}” processes the microphone and plays it on headphones or speakers. “{ownVoice}” and listening to music do not show listener or streaming wording. Switch Use at the top of “{connect}”.
settings.appearanceMotion: Buttons sink slightly only while pressed. A switch thumb, and the mark when choosing one of several options, slide into place. Turning off animation effects in Windows stops the sink and the slide, and leaves the color change. The motion is the same in every theme.
help.trouble.silentBody: Check “{mute}” and “{gain}”. Diagnostics can check input and output status.
help.trouble.receiverBody: Select the input in your destination app that connects to Auralyn’s output device. Check the guides for routing if a virtual cable is needed.
help.trouble.dropoutsBody: Check audio processing status with diagnostics. Increasing the buffer in settings may improve stability, but also increases latency.
help.trouble.keepsRunningBody: Closing the window hides Auralyn in the tray, and the audio keeps running. Choose “Stop Auralyn’s audio” from the status on the top band to stop it. Choose “Quit Auralyn” to quit the app.
help.keys.f1: Press F1 to open “How to use”, including while an input field has focus.
help.keys.fallback: You can check assignments in Settings → Hotkeys.

saveHelp.appliedOnly: Neither saves unapplied drafts or preview candidates. Listen first and confirm application. Saving or registering alone does not switch the sound.
singing.help.lowCutHz: The boundary below which low frequencies are reduced. Hz measures frequency. Raising it removes a wider range of low rumble, but may also thin the voice. Lower it if your voice sounds too thin.
singing.help.dynamics: Reduces louder parts to narrow the difference from quieter parts. 0% leaves this adjustment off; higher values apply stronger reduction. Lower it if singing loses expression. This does not turn up overall microphone volume.
singing.help.brightnessDb: Adjusts the high frequencies of the voice. dB measures the amount of change: 0 is unchanged, positive is brighter, and negative is softer. Lower it if the voice sounds sharp. This is separate from overall volume.
singing.help.mix: The amount of reverb added to the original voice when reverb is enabled. Higher adds more; 0% adds none. Reduce it if words become harder to understand.
singing.help.decaySeconds: An indication of how long the reverb fades. More seconds give a longer tail; fewer give a shorter one. Shorten it if the tail overlaps the next words too much. The sound does not stop abruptly at the specified time.
singing.help.damping: Reduces high frequencies in the reverb. Higher values make the tail darker; lower values make it brighter. Increase it if the reverb sounds sharp. This is separate from the brightness of the voice itself.
singing.help.listen: Change one setting a little at a time, preview, then apply. Opening help alone changes neither values nor stream audio.

recovery.undoScope: These are the scope and restore point for each operation. Fetch the history status to check current availability.
recovery.undo.nr: Noise reduction candidate: restores noise reduction settings from before applying it in Voice Check. Changed conditions can prevent restoration.

peak.title: Reduce loud peaks
peak.lead: Turns down only sudden loud sound, so strong peaks are softer for your ears and the stream.
peak.leadMusic: Turns down only sudden loud sound, so strong peaks are softer for your ears.
peak.scope: Off by default. Limits broadcast and monitor outputs separately after output volume.
peak.scopeMusic: Off by default. After output volume, it limits the sound that reaches your ears.
peak.limitsTitle: Scope of protection, and how long the setting lasts
peak.limits: Sample peaks only. Does not prevent true peaks, clipping already present at input or inside VSTs, or gain added in OBS or calls. Over-limit peaks are attenuated immediately; switching and ceiling changes use 5 ms smoothing and recovery uses the selected release. Recheck recorded sound and the final receiver. Settings stay within the current app and are reapplied when the engine is recreated; app restart resets them to off. Measure fixed-gain proposals with protection off, then recheck the protected final output. Not included in setups or live modes. Independent recording preview is outside this scope. Changes are blocked by control lock.
peak.limitsMusic: Sample peaks only. Does not prevent true peaks, clipping already present at input or inside VSTs, or gain added after the output. Over-limit peaks are attenuated immediately; switching and ceiling changes use 5 ms smoothing and recovery uses the selected release. Loud peaks change the sound, so listen again to the recording and to the sound that reaches your ears. Settings stay within the current app and are reapplied when the engine is recreated; app restart resets them to off. Measure fixed-gain proposals with protection off, then turn protection on and listen again to the sound that reaches your ears. Not saved in setups. Independent recording preview is outside this scope. Changes are blocked by control lock.
peak.failed: Could not confirm the status or application. Review settings, start audio and try again.
peak.liveLocked: Can't be changed while control lock is on. Unlock to change it.
truePeak.title: Broadcast true-peak limit
truePeak.lead: Turns down only sudden loud peaks in the sound sent to the stream, so those peaks are softer.
truePeak.scope: Off by default. It runs only as the last stage of a split broadcast output. Monitor and single-output delay stay unchanged. The guarantee is the estimated true peak of the samples delivered to the broadcast device. Processing inside OBS and sample-rate conversion in the device are outside this scope.
truePeak.latency: Broadcast lookahead: {samples} samples. The monitor path adds 0 samples.
truePeak.notApplied: This applies only to a split broadcast output (not applied now).
truePeak.limitsTitle: Lookahead, and how long the setting lasts
truePeak.limits: Lookahead is about 1.2 ms at 48 kHz. The length follows the sample rate and the delay of the filter that looks between samples. Switching on or off fades briefly, clears the delay line, and fades back in, so that interval is silent. Changing the ceiling does not fade; it only ramps. Ceiling and release are separate from sample-peak protection. Settings stay in the current app and are copied when the engine is recreated. Restarting the app turns this off. Setups and singing/talk modes do not store it. Control lock blocks changes.
truePeak.failed: Could not confirm the status or application. Review settings, start audio and try again.

templates.chatting.name: Just Chatting
templates.chatting.description: A direction that reduces steady noise and narrows differences in voice level.
templates.chatting.slot0.label: Noise gate
templates.chatting.slot0.notes: Reduces steady noise such as PC fans while you are not speaking. Adjust Threshold so it acts during pauses.
templates.chatting.slot1.label: Compressor
templates.chatting.slot1.notes: Reduces differences between quiet and loud speech. A starting example is Ratio 4:1 and about 3–6 dB of gain reduction.
templates.chatting.slot2.label: Limiter
templates.chatting.slot2.notes: An example for controlling loud peaks. Place it last and try a ceiling around −1.0 dB.
templates.singing.name: Singing
templates.singing.description: A direction that shapes the singing range and adds a sense of space.
templates.singing.slot0.label: Equalizer (EQ)
templates.singing.slot0.notes: An example adjustment: cut below 100 Hz and raise 2–4 kHz slightly. This does not guarantee how it will sound.
templates.singing.slot1.label: Compressor
templates.singing.slot1.notes: Evens out singing dynamics. Compare settings by listening; singing may use stronger compression than speech.
templates.singing.slot2.label: Reverb
templates.singing.slot2.notes: Adds a sense of space. Start with a restrained Mix of about 10–20%.
templates.singing.slot3.label: Limiter
templates.singing.slot3.notes: Adjust the ceiling and input level to control peaks. This does not guarantee that clipping is prevented.
templates.ASMR.name: ASMR
templates.ASMR.description: A direction for a close voice that keeps quiet sounds and holds back louder ones. It does not guarantee level limits or hearing protection.
templates.ASMR.slot0.label: Compressor (gentle)
templates.ASMR.slot0.notes: Used to raise quiet sounds. A longer release is a starting point.
templates.ASMR.slot1.label: Limiter (level control)
templates.ASMR.slot1.notes: Check the ceiling and input level, then listen from a low playback level. This does not guarantee device volume or hearing safety.

audioQueue.startupHelp: Startup includes the first read that consumes input. This distinction does not guarantee that the beginning of the audio is intact.
audioQueue.recoveryLimitations: Recovery fades out before removing old complete frames. It does not correct clock-rate differences. No new recovery starts during measurement, recording, preview or global mute.
audioQueue.units: A frame contains all channels; a slot is one sample of one channel. Time conversion uses the attempt’s actual output rate. This is queued audio duration, not signal transit time from input to output. It is not added to calculated or reported latency.
audioQueue.limitations: Includes shortages just after startup. Shortage filling counts only audio queue reads and is separate from mute or failure silence. Concurrent updates may cause observation differences while running; maxima cover only observed values. Bounded recovery may remove old frames. Ongoing device clock differences are not corrected; ASRC is not performed. Corresponding-frame timing is shown separately.

frameTiming.title: Corresponding-frame read timing
frameTiming.pendingScope: Pending joins include records not yet collected and correspondence still awaiting a decision.
frameTiming.limitations: Observes from input callback arrival to completion of the audio queue read containing corresponding frames. All frames in a callback share a timestamp. Actual signal timing through noise reduction, VSTs, reverb, previews or test tones, and total transit to devices or OBS, are unmeasured. Not added to calculated or reported values. Missing metadata does not cause audio to wait or be thinned.

gpuiShell.offUntilOn: You can choose the type and amount while it stays off. The sound does not change until you turn it on.
gpuiShell.noiseModeFirst: The noise reduction type is unknown. Choose Low or High to apply on/off, strength and voice protection.
gpuiShell.hotkeyFailed: Some shortcuts could not be registered (Auralyn may be running). Check the Settings page.
gpuiShell.peakResets: When you restart the app, it turns off and the ceiling and release return to their defaults.
gpuiShell.setupScope: Saving and applying cover the VST chain, noise reduction and the voice chain. Devices and sample rate stay as they are.
gpuiShell.setupImportExists: A setup named “{arg0}” already exists, so the file was not imported.
gpuiShell.setupImportNothing: This file has no VST chain, noise reduction or voice shaping settings, so it was not imported.
gpuiShell.setupImportInvalid: This file could not be read as a setup.
gpuiShell.shortcutsUnreadable: Could not read the saved shortcuts, so none are registered
gpuiShell.shortcutsEditInTauri: For now, change keys in the Tauri version settings (they share the same file). Restart the GPUI version after changing them.
gpuiShell.liveInactive: The stream output is stopped. To change the output, stop audio, save, then start again.
gpuiShell.liveSplitKept: For now, fine-tune your own singing and talk shaping in the Tauri version. The first time you separate them, defaults are used; existing values are kept.
gpuiShell.mixNeedOutput: First, on the Connect page, choose a stream output under "Separate for yourself and the stream", turn on separate processing, and save.
gpuiShell.setupLead: Choose what it is for, and a likely microphone and output are picked for you. Change them if they are wrong.
gpuiShell.setupOther: Choose ASIO and others on the Connect page
gpuiShell.helpSilentBody: Check that audio is running on the top band, that “{emergency}” is off in the right column, and that “{gain}” is not 0.
gpuiShell.helpDropoutsBody: Check processing delays and dropouts under “{diagnostics}” on this page. A larger buffer on the Connect page may be more stable, but adds delay.
gpuiShell.helpKeepsRunningBody: Closing the window with × hides it in the notification area, and the audio keeps running. To stop it, choose “{stop}” on the top band. To quit, choose “{quit}” from the notification area icon.
gpuiShell.helpReceiverBody: Set the input of the destination app (OBS, Discord and so on) to the device that Auralyn’s output reaches. “Learn more” explains how to connect a virtual cable.
gpuiShell.modesSaveSinging: Register the current sound as singing
gpuiShell.modesSaveTalk: Register the current sound as talk
gpuiShell.modesHint: Switches only the registered voice shaping and reverb. The microphone, VSTs, noise reduction, volume and mute stay as they are.
gpuiShell.modesRegisterNote: Registers the voice shaping and reverb in use now. For talk, the reverb is registered as off.
gpuiShell.modesLinked: Switch modes that are linked to a VST setup in the previous version.
gpuiShell.modesLocked: This can't be done while operations are locked. Unlock with “Lock controls” on the Sound page, then try again.
gpuiShell.themeSaveFailed: The theme changed for this session, but could not be saved. It may reset when you reopen the app.
gpuiShell.recoverySafety: Your saved VST rack is kept. Excluded VSTs, or all VSTs when you resume without them, stay in the rack as not-loaded slots and are loaded again the next time the app starts. To drop the VST that caused it, delete its slot on the VST page. After resuming, check the audio and the receiving app separately.
gpuiShell.themeNote: Only the colors change here. The cut corners and italic headings of Gaming are only in the previous version.
